title: Integrated transcriptomics prioritizes cell types and genes associated with MASH fibrosis
summary: Junjie Zhang and colleagues at Gannan Medical University and affiliated institutions combined four bulk RNA-sequencing datasets, a single-nucleus liver dataset and machine-learning feature selection to identify fibrosis-associated genes and cell populations in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH). They report a seven-gene signature with AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.69–0.93) in an independent cohort, and qRT-PCR checks of selected genes in a methionine-choline-deficient mouse model. These results support candidate associations; mouse expression checks do not establish causal mechanisms or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Robust rank aggregation, WGCNA and machine-learning feature selection with single-nucleus RNA sequencing
organization: Gannan Medical University; The Affiliated Fifth People’s Hospital of Ganzhou, Gannan Medical University

evidence.tested: A seven-gene signature achieved AUC 0.81 (95% CI 0.69–0.93) in an independent cohort within the study; selected expression directions were checked by qRT-PCR in a MASH mouse model.
evidence.unknown: Gene associations and mouse expression validation do not establish causality, therapeutic effect or clinical utility.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning feature selection prioritized fibrosis-associated genes from integrated bulk transcriptomics; single-nucleus analysis characterized cell populations and qRT-PCR checked selected expression in mice.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text reviewed for title, authorship, Methods, Results, version date and stated limitations.
